newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HSBC rules out Australia bank buy.
newsitem.headline: HSBC rules out Australia bank buy.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc's group chairman Sir William Purves said the banking group did not have an acquisition "shopping list" involving Australian banks.
"We don't have a shopping list and I don't have Australia on any list at all at this time," Purves told Channel Nine Business Sunday television programme.
He had been asked if the bank's expansion plans included takeovers or mergers.
HSBC's Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp has been speculated upon as a possible bidder for one of the "Big Four" Australian banks.
"We're a huge group already. Everybody seems to think we should be buying something more," Purves said.
He said the group's intention in Australia was to grow its current business, HongkongBank of Australia Ltd.
"In our own way it probably means we will not be a huge player for a very long time, if at all, but that's the way we intend to go about it," he said.

Asked if he was concerned about the possibility of Chinese companies buying heavily into the bank as they had into other major Hong Kong companies, Purves said there was no real reason for comparing banks with airlines and phone companies.
Purves said Chinese banks have around 25 percent of the banking market in Hong Kong and HSBC had come under no pressure from China.
"The media keep telling me that we're going sell some part of the Hang Seng Bank," he said.
"The board has made it very clear that investment is one of the best investments that we have and it's not for sale," he said.
